To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
plasmasphere density is a function of solar wind speed and that this function can be described by a simple power-law relation.
the plasmasphere total electron content (NP), as measured by a radio beacon technique, decreases with increasing solar wind speed (Vsw) and vice versa.

the total plasmaspheric electron content is found to increase with decreasing solar wind speed during magnetic storms, and that the increase in NP is associated with a decrease of the convection electric-field strength.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between the total plasmaspheric electron content and the solar wind speed.
the effect of the solar wind on plasmasphere behaviour.
the effect on NP of solar-wind speed variations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the solar wind influences the plasmasphere through its influence on the electric field in the magnetosphere.
the total plasmaspheric electron content is a decreasing function of the solar-wind speed.
the plasmaspheric electron content NP increases with decrease in solar wind speed Vsw.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NP and Vsw are inversely related.
the solar wind is a dominant factor influencing NP.
the plasmasphere is a dynamic entity which is strongly affected by solar wind speed and magnetic field variations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the solar wind influences plasmaphere electron content.
the plasmasphere responds rapidly to changes in the solar wind speed.
NP is not only dependent on L but also on solar wind speed Vsw.
